absent: Vendor hook behavior for starting bypass and updating interrupt remapping entries.
Translation from MSI routing entry to LAPIC fields and trigger-mode encoding.
Hyper-V routing effects and predicates for split, in-kernel and bypass-capable irqchips.
APIC presence, destination matching and cached map construction rules.
Helpers for IOAPIC scanning, PIC output refresh and IOAPIC state access.
Consumers of reverse chip maps and handling of multi-entry GSI fan-out.
Remaining emulation callbacks beyond the truncated fragment and their error contracts.
Tracepoint format and sequence-counter reader protocol for irqfd entries.
PIC selector logic and arbitration between PIC and IOAPIC delivery.

findings.text: Host helpers expose IOAPIC route rescanning for a vCPU plus a hook invoked after routing table replacement, with an x86-specific behavior and a generic fallback that performs no action.
Interrupt bypass exposes producer attach and detach operations plus a per-irqfd routing refresh hook, with a generic weak refresh that performs no action when the architecture provides no override.
Routing management exposes installation of a user-supplied table, global refresh of attached irqfds, and installation of a legacy default mapping covering low global numbers.

VM control operations provide retrieval and replacement of master PIC, slave PIC and IOAPIC state selected by a chip identifier, rejecting unknown identifiers and refreshing derived PIC output after replacement.

Rescan is bounded by the smaller of the current table extent and the reserved IOAPIC pin count, considers only MSI entries, and contributes only those whose translated LAPIC form carries an asserted trigger mode to the handled-vector set.
Direct posting is permitted only for fixed and lowest-priority delivery modes; any other delivery mode, or a destination that is not a single vCPU, forces remapped handling with no bypass target.

Posted-interrupt table programming requires an in-kernel irqchip together with bypass support, leaves state unchanged when both prior and new bypass targets are absent, and otherwise delegates to the vendor hook while recording the selected bypass vCPU.

Single-destination determination holds exactly when one present vCPU matches the destination; shorthand always bypasses the cached map, the cached map may decide early on a singleton bitmap entry, otherwise presence plus destination matching over all vCPUs decides.

Producer attachment records the producer and maintains a count of bypass-capable sources that starts vendor bypassing on first arrival and rolls back on MSI programming failure; detachment reverts to remapped mode, clears the producer and decrements the count.
Per-irqfd routing refresh ignores transitions where neither side is MSI and ignores MSI to MSI transitions with identical payload; all other transitions reprogram posted-interrupt state.
Default legacy mapping assigns low global numbers to both IOAPIC and PIC delivery with PIC selection and pin folding for the low range, while higher legacy numbers are IOAPIC only.

Table installation rejects out-of-range global numbers and illegal flag combinations, sizes the table from the highest presented global number, initializes reverse chip lookups to empty, builds each entry through a per-entry constructor, then publishes atomically and waits for prior readers before freeing the old table.

Per-entry construction enforces at most one mapping between a global number and a given irqchip and at most one non-irqchip mapping per global number, records reverse chip to global translation, and links the entry into the per-global bucket.
Irqfd refresh maps its global number to current entries and preserves a usable routing only when exactly one entry matches; any other cardinality clears the type to indicate no routable target.

Routing readers rely on SRCU, cached APIC map readers rely on RCU, table publication serializes with a mutex followed by expedited SRCU quiescence, irqfd list and producer state serialize with an IRQ-safe spinlock, PIC state serializes with its own spinlock, and per-irqfd routing snapshots publish under a sequence counter with lock-held assertion.

Virtual PIC state pairs per-channel request, mask, service, edge, priority, base, mode and sequencing fields plus a back link with a container holding a lock, wakeup flag, pending acknowledgment count, VM link, master and slave channels, derived output level, three IO devices and a per-pin level array.

Fault record carries a vector, error-code presence plus value, nested fault indication, overlapping storage usable as fault address or debug state or payload, an async fault marker and an exit qualification value.

Decoded instruction record carries intercept kind, prefix presence, decomposed addressing fields, source and destination values with widths and kinds, address width, and current plus following instruction addresses.

Emulation callback table groups processor state access, standard and fetched and emulated memory access with atomic compare exchange, invalidation, port IO, segment and descriptor table handling, control and debug registers, filtered MSR and counter access, halt and cache and hypercall and intercept hooks, and CPUID plus feature queries; the visible fragment is explicitly partial.
Legacy PIC pin count is sixteen and sizes the per-pin level storage.

Emulation outcome codes are zero for continue, one for unhandleable, two for fault propagation, three for instruction retry, four for failed compare exchange, five for IO needed, six for nested interception, and seven for unhandleable vectoring.

Emulation access attributes are single-bit flags with write as bit zero, fetch as bit one, implicit access as bit two, invalidation as bit three, MSR access as bit four, and descriptor-table load as bit five.

Loss warnings are suppressed when an in-kernel PIC may have consumed the interrupt or when Xen emulation is enabled; bypass programming warns on missing irqchip capability and on clearing an active bypass target after vendor failure, detachment warns on producer mismatch and on remnant bypass state for non-MSI entries, and unknown chip selectors or illegal routing inputs fail cleanly.

A bypass-capable source rests detached, becomes attached in remapped mode when its producer appears without an eligible single posted target, moves to posted mode when an MSI route yields a single postable vCPU, and returns to remapped or detached on routing change, producer removal or programming failure.

Generic weak hooks for post-replacement notification and per-irqfd refresh perform no action; x86 overrides add Hyper-V notification plus split-irqchip rescan requests and MSI-aware posted-interrupt reprogramming.

Assembly offset helper emits vendor-specific field offsets for register state, current control structures, speculation control and saved-state addresses, gated by AMD and Intel build selection, under a compilation marker.
Header markers provide single-inclusion protection for IRQ and emulation definitions.
